## What this is

A read-only client for one Moodle site. It pulls everything a course holds ---
deadlines, submission state, grades, files, and the rules buried in PDFs and
HTML pages --- and reduces it to **one JSON document per course** in SQLite.

The problem it solves: Moodle's API answers what a course keeps in *fields*.
How a module is graded, which sessions require physical attendance, and what
the final exam covers are almost never fields. They are sentences in a
syllabus PDF, a line in a semester-plan screenshot, or a forum announcement.
So the project has two halves: pull the fields, then read the documents with a
model and fill the gaps the fields left.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Built against `moodle.zhaw.ch` (SWITCH edu-ID SSO). Nothing in the code is
ZHAW-specific beyond `DEFAULT_SITE` --- any Moodle with the mobile web service
enabled should work.
:::

## Pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph auth["1 · Auth"]
    A["SSO in a browser<br/>→ web-service token<br/>→ OS keyring"]
  end
  subgraph pull["2 · Pull"]
    B["Structured sync<br/><i>fields → JSON document</i>"]
    C["Harvest<br/><i>prose + files → corpus/</i>"]
  end
  subgraph read["3 · Read (LLM)"]
    D["Pass 1 · Screen<br/><i>which documents<br/>describe the rules?</i>"]
    E["Pass 2 · Extract<br/><i>grading, attendance,<br/>missing activities</i>"]
  end
  F[("moodle.sqlite<br/>one doc per course")]

  A --> B
  A --> C
  B --> F
  C --> D --> E
  E -->|"additive merge"| F

  classDef llm fill:#eef3fb,stroke:#7fa8d8
  class D,E llm
```

Stages 2 and 3 are independent of each other up to the merge: the structured
sync never needs a model, and the model never writes a field the API already
answered. See [Extraction](extraction.qmd) for why that boundary is enforced in
code rather than in a prompt.

## Repository layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/config.py` | Every tunable value: endpoints, paths, budgets, prompts. No logic. |
| `src/logs.py` | [Session logging](logging.qmd): one file per application start. |
| `src/auth/` | `flow.py` --- the SSO token handshake. `tokens.py` --- keyring persistence. |
| `src/data_retention/client.py` | REST client. Allowlists 25 read-only functions; turns Moodle's HTTP-200 errors into exceptions. |
| `src/data_retention/session.py` | One authenticated connection. Login, token reuse, every typed pull. |
| `src/data_retention/activities.py` | Per-module record shapes (quiz, assign, workshop, lesson) and field coercion. |
| `src/data_retention/progress.py` | Per-user state: attempts, submissions, completion. |
| `src/data_retention/document.py` | Builds the one-JSON-document-per-course shape from the pulled records. |
| `src/data_retention/corpus.py` | Harvests prose and files verbatim to a corpus directory with a manifest. |
| `src/extraction/documents.py` | Turns corpus files into model-readable content blocks, or records why not. |
| `src/extraction/screen.py` | Pass 1: relevance verdict per document. |
| `src/extraction/extract.py` | Pass 2: one proposal per course, with provenance. |
| `src/extraction/merge.py` | Applies a proposal additively. Cannot overwrite. |
| `src/storage/sqlite.py` | The table, the activities view, and the queries. |

Driver scripts at the repository root (`*_test.py`) are thin CLIs over these
modules --- useful as worked examples of the call order.

## Running it

```bash
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium     # for the SSO capture

uv run python main_test.py             # stage 2: structured sync only
uv run python harvest_test.py          # stage 3: harvest documents
uv run python screen_test.py           # stage 4: pass 1  (costs API tokens)
uv run python extract_test.py          # stage 5: pass 2  (costs API tokens)

uv run python pipeline_test.py          # all of the above, end to end
uv run python pipeline_test.py --skip-llm   # stages 1-3 only, spends nothing
```

The database is rebuilt on every run, since the structured sync is a handful
of calls. The corpus is **updated in place**: a file is downloaded only when
Moodle reports a new `timemodified` or size, a text is rewritten only when its
content changed, and whatever a course no longer lists is deleted, so what is
on disk is still what Moodle holds now. Passes 1 and 2 then reuse their
results for content whose `sha256` is unchanged, so an unchanged course costs
no tokens. The dashboard's Sync button asks each time whether to pull only
what changed or do a full rebuild, which clears the corpus and its screening
and extraction reports and pulls and reads everything again
(`POST /api/sync` with `{"full_rebuild": true}`). `SYNC_REBUILDS_FROM_SCRATCH`
in `src/config.py` is the default when a request does not say.

Outputs, all in the project directory and all gitignored:

| Artefact | Written by |
|---|---|
| `moodle.sqlite` | stage 2, extended by stage 5 |
| `course_documents.txt` | stage 2 --- the same documents, pretty-printed |
| `corpus/<id>-<shortname>/` | stage 3 --- raw HTML and files |
| `corpus/manifest.json` | stage 3 --- provenance for every harvested item |
| `corpus/screening.json` | stage 4 --- one verdict per document |
| `corpus/extraction.json` | stage 5 --- proposals, merge results, token usage |
| `logs/modboard-<time>-<pid>.log` | every start of the app --- see [Logging](logging.qmd) |

## Scale of one real run

Five favourite courses on a ZHAW autumn semester:

| | |
|---|---|
| Harvested | 37 prose items, 206 files (210 MB), 23 links, 0 warnings |
| Screened | 243 documents → 211 model calls, 30 decided on format, 2 unreadable |
| Relevant | 32 documents (1.07 M input tokens, 62 s at 8 workers) |
| Extracted | 31 additions applied, 0 rejected, 0 conflicts (37 s at 3 workers) |

## What is built, and what is not

| Layer | Covers | State |
|---|---|---|
| Auth | SSO token capture, signature verification, keyring | Built |
| Course set | Favourites, metadata, lecturers, capability flags | Built |
| Deadlines | Quiz, assignment, workshop, lesson dates | Built |
| Personal state | Quiz attempts and grades, assignment submissions | Built |
| Harvest | Sections, intros, pages, labels, blocks, forums, files | Built |
| Pass 1 / Pass 2 | Screening, extraction, additive merge | Built |
| Gradebook | Per-activity grades outside quizzes; any grade *scale* | Not pulled |
| Component ↔ activity link | Which activities make up a grading component | Not modelled |
| Completion | `session.completion()` exists but is not written into the document | Wired up partially |

The last three are the known gaps, and they are the ones a frontend runs into
first. A grading component carries a weight but no list of the activities that
satisfy it, and `grade_achieved` is populated for quizzes only --- for
assignments, workshops and lessons `document.py` leaves it `null` with the
comment *"needs the gradebook; not pulled yet"*. Any UI showing a current grade
has to stop at percent-of-max per quiz.
